title: Optimal Load Balancing for Finite Heterogeneous Parallel-Server Queues
short_statement: For a finite system of parallel queues with heterogeneous service rates, characterize an optimal dispatching policy or prove structural optimality of a simple speed-aware rule.
open_problem: In the heterogeneous case, the open problem is to characterize an optimal finite-system dispatching rule, or to prove/disprove optimality of a natural speed-aware index/JSQ rule.
background: Load balancing is one of the basic controls in service systems, call centers, cloud computing, and data-center scheduling. The homogeneous-server model is classical: routing to the shortest queue has strong optimality properties because servers are exchangeable. Heterogeneous service rates remove that symmetry. A fast server with a longer queue may dominate a slow idle server, but the correct tradeoff depends on the whole queue vector and future arrivals. This makes the finite-system dynamic program natural but hard to understand structurally. The problem is well defined and not primarily about model choice: arrivals, exponential services, observable queues, and a standard holding-cost objective give a concrete continuous-time Markov decision process. The research gap is that the field has increasingly sharp asymptotic policies, while the exact finite-system decision rule remains unknown except in special cases.
full_statement: Consider $m$ parallel single-server queues. Jobs arrive according to a Poisson process and must be routed immediately and irrevocably to one server. Server $i$ works at exponential rate $\mu_i$, with possibly unequal service rates. A dispatching policy observes the queue-length vector $Q(t)=(Q_1(t),\ldots,Q_m(t))$ and server speeds $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_m$, and chooses the destination server for each arrival. For a finite system with fixed $m$ and fixed rates, the objective may be to minimize steady-state mean response time, steady-state expected total queue length, or the discounted/average-cost Markov decision problem with holding cost $\sum_i Q_i(t)$. In the homogeneous case $\mu_i\equiv\mu$, Join-the-Shortest-Queue is optimal for standard objectives. In the heterogeneous case, the open problem is to characterize an optimal finite-system dispatching rule, or to prove/disprove optimality of a natural speed-aware index/JSQ rule. Recent work proves asymptotic optimality of speed-aware JSQ in large-system fluid and Halfin-Whitt regimes, but those limit theorems do not settle exact finite-system optimality.
known_results: For identical servers, JSQ minimizes standard delay metrics. For heterogeneous systems, Bhambay and Mukhopadhyay prove fluid-limit delay optimality of Speed-Aware JSQ, and Bhambay, Buke, and Mukhopadhyay prove asymptotic optimality in the Halfin-Whitt regime, including steady-state diffusion-scaled optimality among policies using queue lengths and server speeds. Zhou, Shroff, and Wierman resolve a related delayed-information open problem in large heterogeneous systems through an asymptotically optimal local-estimation-driven framework. These results do not identify an exact optimal dispatching policy for a fixed finite heterogeneous system.

progress.summary: Large-system fluid and Halfin-Whitt optimality results support speed-aware JSQ-type policies. The exact finite Markov decision problem and its structural optimal policy remain open.

counterexample_rationale: A small finite system with two or three heterogeneous servers can refute a proposed simple index rule. Exact dynamic-programming computation on truncated state spaces can generate candidate counterexamples, though proof requires bounding truncation or solving the MDP exactly.
alphaevolve_rationale: Automated search can compare candidate dispatching rules against finite-state dynamic programs and discover threshold structures or counterexamples. This is a good target for code-assisted conjecture formation.

literature.synthesis: The finite homogeneous problem has strong monotonicity and exchangeability, making JSQ optimal. Heterogeneity breaks exchangeability and creates a speed-delay tradeoff that is easy to state but hard to solve. Recent papers take an asymptotic route: speed-aware JSQ is delay optimal in fluid limits and remains optimal in Halfin-Whitt heavy traffic, with steady-state interchange justified by Stein and Lyapunov arguments. Related work handles multiple dispatchers and delayed information in large systems. What remains is the finite-system structural problem: identify the exact optimal action regions in queue-length space, or prove that no simple index/threshold characterization can hold generally.

reviewed.ref: Sanidhay Bhambay, Burak Buke, Arpan Mukhopadhyay, 'Asymptotic Optimality of the Speed-Aware Join-the-Shortest-Queue in the Halfin-Whitt Regime for Heterogeneous Systems', arXiv 2024
reviewed.result: Proves Halfin-Whitt steady-state optimality of SA-JSQ and explicitly notes finite optimality remains open.

reviewed.ref: Xingyu Zhou, Ness Shroff, Adam Wierman, 'Asymptotically Optimal Load Balancing in Large-scale Heterogeneous Systems with Multiple Dispatchers', arXiv 2020
reviewed.result: Gives asymptotically optimal policies for heterogeneous systems with multiple dispatchers and delayed local estimates.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Analyze the continuous-time MDP for two heterogeneous servers first, looking for monotone switching curves. Use value iteration on truncated state spaces to formulate conjectures, then prove them through coupling, submodularity, or dynamic-programming inequalities.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: A claimed optimal policy must specify the objective and prove optimality for the untruncated infinite-state system. Numerical MDP evidence is useful only as conjecture support unless accompanied by rigorous truncation bounds.
